newsitem.title: USA: Cephalon aims to submit NDAs by year-end.
newsitem.headline: Cephalon aims to submit NDAs by year-end.

text.p: Cephalon Inc President Frank Baldino told investors the firm hopes to submit New Drug Application (NDA) filings for Myotrophin and Provigil by the end of 1996.

"A nice goal for us would be an NDA for both these drugs by the end of the year and we are working hard to make that happen," Baldino said in a presentation to the Montgomery Securities investment conference here.

The West Chester, Pennsylvania biopharmaceutical company and its partner Chiron Corp in June received U.S. Food and Drug Administration clearance for a Treatment Investigational New Drug (T-IND) early access program for use of Myotrophin in patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), also known as Lou Gehrig's disease, in the U.S. market.

Asked whether the company may have further financing needs in the future, the chief executive said that would depend on a range of factors, including its ability to bring products to market and whether it decides to develop or acquire other businesses.

"If both drugs get approved, which we fully expect, we should be in a profitability mode in the 1998 time frame," Baldino said, adding that without other business opportunities and decisions their earnings would make such financing unneeded.
As of the end of its second quarter June 30, Cephalon had approximately $155 million in cash and marketable securities.

Provigil is a drug candidate for the treatment of excessive daytime sleepiness associated with narcolepsy. The company is also conducting Phase II clinical studies of Myotrophin in post-polio syndrome and peripheral neuropathies.

The company's product pipeline includes half a dozen other potential products and it currently markets two products in the United States for the treatment of neurological conditions, under an agreement with Bristol-Myers Squibb Co.
